_comment: One attempt to reproduce one run's number, and everything the verdict rests on. Written by scripts/repro/repro.py; this template documents the shape and is what a manual fallback must reproduce. Lives at {PROJECT}/repro/{session_id}/session.json — project-level rather than under a stage, because a session routinely spans two: reproducing a TRAINING number is normally done by re-running EVAL against the surviving checkpoint, so its trials are eval runs and its target is a training run. Like a handoff it has no `steps` block; unlike a census it is not a dated observation you can retake, because its trials cost GPU hours and are its evidence.
_comment_status: open | closed. A session that ran out of budget while still `inconclusive` stays OPEN with what it has. Closing it would freeze a non-answer into the record as if it were an answer.
_comment_target: The run being reproduced and the number being reproduced. `mode` and `scope` are copied here at open, not read live, because they are what every trial gets checked against — run-mechanics 'Metric comparability'. A target with mode: null is refused at open: metrics are comparable only within the same mode and an equivalent scope, so nothing could be shown to be the same quantity.
_comment_measure_via: eval | retrain. How the number gets re-measured, and `eval` is the default even when the target is a training run. Retraining to verify a number costs what the original cost and answers a fuzzier question, because nondeterminism means the best available answer is a band rather than a match; re-measuring the surviving checkpoint through eval answers 'is the recorded number real' for the price of one eval. `retrain` answers a different and rarer question — 'does this recipe still produce a model this good' — and open refuses it without --i-accept-the-cost.
_comment_probe: Fixed inputs run through BOTH the original artifact and each reproduction, rendered side by side for a person. Declared at open and never afterwards: a probe set chosen once the result is known is a test written to its own answer. Ideally a citation (datasets/<id>@<snapshot>) so membership is pinned too. 20-50 units is plenty — this is a look, not an eval. Null when no probe was declared, in which case the prediction half of the verdict is simply absent rather than assumed.
_comment_declared_tolerance: The expectation, recorded before any trial runs. It does NOT decide the verdict — `band` does. It is kept so the two can be compared: a declared tolerance wider than the measured spread would have accepted a divergence larger than real noise, and one tighter than the spread would have called the pipeline's own noise a divergence. Either finding lands in `caveats`.
_comment_axes_at_open: The five-axis verdict at the moment the session opened, one word each: intact | drifted | gone | unverifiable. Snapshotted rather than re-read at close, because close's refusals are about the conditions the trials actually ran under. `axes_detail_at_open` holds the full probe output behind them.
_comment_trials: One entry per completed run registered as a trial. Entry: {n, run, stage, pinned[], value, delta, delta_pct, probe_run, predictions_agree, at}. `pinned` empty = a band trial (nothing changed); a named axis = an attribution trial with that axis pinned back to what the original recorded. Every trial is an ORDINARY run in stages/<stage>/runs/, visible to list_runs.py and build_dag.py, and carries lineage.repro_of pointing at the target — deliberately not fork_of, since a fork intends to differ and a trial intends to be identical.
_comment_band: The interval the unpinned repeats actually produced: {n, min, max, mean, spread, target, target_inside, nearest_edge_gap, measured_at, from_trials[]}. Null until at least 3 unpinned trials exist — two points are a range, not a band. No distribution is assumed and none is needed: 'would this pipeline have produced that number again' is answered by whether it did.
_comment_metric_verdict: reproduced (target inside the interval) | inconclusive (outside, but within one spread of the edge — run more repeats) | diverged (further out than the whole spread). `inconclusive` is not a hedge, it is the loop's engine.
_comment_predictions_agree: Whether the probe outputs agree, judged by a PERSON from the side-by-side — not by an epsilon. 'The boxes moved 0.3px' and 'the small objects vanished' are both numeric differences and no threshold on a prediction file separates them, which is the entire reason this is a look. Per /ask-human's rule the judgement is a claim; record on what basis it was made in `caveats`. Null means no probe was run, which is a third state and must not read as true.
_comment_attributed_to: data | code | env | params | artifacts — the axis whose pinning brought the number back into range while the others did not. Null on every verdict except `diverged`, which refuses to close without it.
_comment_verdict: reproduced | reproduced_with_drift | metric_ok_predictions_diverged | diverged | diverged_unattributed | not_reproducible. `reproduced` requires a band, every axis intact, and agreeing predictions; anything less is reproduced_with_drift, which is a weaker fact that has to keep saying so every time it is read. There is deliberately no verdict for `inconclusive`.
_comment_caveats: Qualifications stamped in automatically at close — every drifted axis, every unverifiable axis, and the tolerance-versus-reality note. They exist so the conclusion carries its own limits wherever it is quoted later, which is the whole reason this record exists: a repro verdict is written once and read by people who can no longer re-check it.
